message.reasoning:
I need to choose between mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE or declaring bankruptcy to cover the $600 rent owed to p1.

Mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE for $120 would cover the $218 shortfall. I have $382 cash after mortgaging KENTUCKY_AVENUE.

Mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE would still leave a $98 shortfall. I cannot cover the full $600 rent with mortgaged assets alone.

I must liquidate all mortgageable assets before declaring bankruptcy. I will mortgage ILLINOIS_AVENUE.

Mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE would still leave a $98 shortfall. I am weighing whether to declare bankruptcy now, since the engine will re-prompt anyway. In bankruptcy, mortgaged properties are worth less than unmortgaged ones.

Mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE would still leave a $98 shortfall. Since I cannot raise enough cash, declaring bankruptcy is valid under the rules.

I see a conflict between the prior rule requiring full liquidation before bankruptcy and the current legal options. Both actions are available, so I must decide whether to mortgage ILLINOIS_AVENUE first or declare bankruptcy now.

I will declare bankruptcy now. The scenario note explicitly permits it when cash cannot be raised. If I mortgage Illinois first, I would still owe $600 and face another prompt with no mortgageable assets left.

I will mortgage ILLINOIS_AVENUE. The engine will re-prompt for bankruptcy after that.

I am checking whether p1 already owns a full orange monopoly. If so, giving them an unmortgaged Illinois Avenue would let them complete the red set.

Neither p1 nor p4 currently owns any red properties, so bankrupting to p1 would not complete a red set. Mortgaging ILLINOIS_AVENUE would give p1 the $120 cash raised, but they would still need to pay 10% interest to unmortgage it.
